{
  "topic": "Model Capabilities Trade-offs",
  "audience": "local LLM enthusiasts",
  "problem_or_goal": "Discuss the observed trade-off between world knowledge and problem-solving abilities in recent smaller LLMs.",
  "context": "An archived Reddit post from May 2, 2025, discusses observations about the performance of various LLMs, specifically noting a potential decline in world knowledge despite improvements in coding and problem-solving benchmarks for newer, smaller models.",
  "motivation": "Understanding if there's a general trend of sacrificing world knowledge for improved problem-solving in smaller LLMs is crucial for users selecting models for diverse tasks.",
  "desired_response": "A discussion exploring the source author's observations, potential reasons for this trend, and whether other enthusiasts have noticed similar patterns or have strategies for evaluating these trade-offs.",
  "speaker_relationship_to_source": "reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests",
  "facts": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "text": "The source author observed that despite rising benchmark scores and claims of equivalence to larger older models, newer smaller models sometimes exhibit worse world knowledge than their predecessors or even lower-benchmarking models of similar size.",
      "evidence_quote": "I've noticed a trend where despite benchmark scores going up and companies claiming that their new small models are equivalent to older much bigger models, world knowledge of these new smaller models is worse than their larger predecessors, and often times worse than lower benchmarking models of similar sizes.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "text": "Newer models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 reportedly show significant improvements in coding and problem-solving compared to older models, but their world knowledge is not better and can be worse than some older models of similar size.",
      "evidence_quote": "New models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 are vastly better at coding and problem solving than older models, but their knowledge is no better than older models and actually worse than some other similar sized older models.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "text": "Specific examples suggest Qwen 3 8B has considerably worse world knowledge than Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B, and Qwen 3 14B has worse world knowledge than Phi 4 and Gemma 3 12B.",
      "evidence_quote": "For example, Qwen 3 8B has considerably worse world knowledge in my tests than old models like Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B. Likewise, Qwen 3 14B has much worse world knowledge than older weaker benchmarking models like Phi 4 and Gemma 3 12B.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "text": "Granite 3.3 is noted to have slightly better coding/problem-solving but slightly worse knowledge compared to Granite 3.2.",
      "evidence_quote": "On a similar note, Granite 3.3 has slightly better coding/problem solving but slightly worse knowledge than Granite 3.2.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "text": "Gemma 3 is described as having slightly better knowledge density than Gemma 2, alongside much better coding and problem-solving, though it's still primarily a knowledge and writing model.",
      "evidence_quote": "There are some exceptions to this trend though. Gemma 3 seems to have slightly better knowledge density than Gemma 2, while also having much better coding and problem solving. Gemma 3 is still very much a knowledge and writing model, and not particularly good at coding or problem solving, but much better at that than Gemma 2.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F6",
      "text": "Llama 4 Maverick is highlighted for its superb world knowledge, surpassing Qwen 3 235B-A22 and DeepSeek V3 in the author's tests, though its coding and problem-solving abilities are considered mediocre.",
      "evidence_quote": "Llama 4 Maverick has superb world knowledge, much better than Qwen 3 235B-A22, and actually slightly better than DeepSeek V3 in my tests, but its coding and problem solving abilities are mediocre.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F7",
      "text": "The source author speculates that the observed trend might be due to training data shifts, with newer models potentially having more problem-solving content and proportionally less knowledge-dense content.",
      "evidence_quote": "My guess is that this is because the training data for new models has more problem solving content and so proportionately less knowledge dense content.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F8",
      "text": "LLM makers may have stopped publishing or highlighting scores for knowledge benchmarks like SimpleQA because those scores are not improving and might be declining.",
      "evidence_quote": "LLM makers have stopped publishing or highlighting scores for knowledge benchmarks like SimpleQA because those scores aren't improving and may be getting worse.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    }
  ],
  "allowed_claims": [
    "The source author observed a potential trade-off between world knowledge and problem-solving abilities in newer, smaller LLMs.",
    "Specific models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 were mentioned as examples of this trend.",
    "Gemma 3 and Llama 4 Maverick were noted as exceptions or counterpoints to the general trend.",
    "The source author hypothesized about the cause being changes in training data composition."
  ],
  "forbidden_claims": [
    "The source author's observations are universally true for all LLMs.",
    "The specific benchmark scores or exact performance metrics mentioned are independently verified.",
    "The models discussed are currently the absolute best or worst in any category.",
    "The source author has personally conducted all mentioned tests on their own hardware.",
    "The trend described is a permanent characteristic of LLM development."
  ],
  "essential_limitations": [
    "The observations are based on the source author's private test questions and specific models tested.",
    "The exact hardware, software versions, and detailed configurations used for testing are not provided.",
    "The specific 'private test questions' are not detailed, making independent replication impossible.",
    "The source date is May 2, 2025, meaning the information reflects the state of LLMs at that time."
  ],
  "missing_information": [
    "Details of the source author's testing methodology and specific prompts.",
    "Exact benchmark scores or quantitative data for knowledge and problem-solving.",
    "Information on the training data composition for the models discussed.",
    "Confirmation of these trends from other independent sources or benchmarks.",
    "Specific model versions beyond what is mentioned (e.g., exact Qwen 3 version)."
  ]
}
